title: The game workbench for your coding AI: Since it’s gotten harder to code games with Claude, I created a companion workbench for coding assistants for games
author: LegoFighter2
selftext:
Think of it as the SAP for game creation..  
  
I had this idea a while back ago, but I saw that a lot of people with no prior software engineering knowledge struggle to create more complex games. 

To save tokens and stop reinventing the wheel on every project, your AI can now reuse from my collection.

Since I see what is used, I can further optimise and enhance what is used often.

Add the MCP to your assistant, and it offers you a huge library of industry best practices and opinionated approaches for your game ideas. 

It also has an idea generator in case you lack ideas. 

You have to bring your own assets, or use ChatGPT or Gemini since they have image gen capabilities...

[https://spielerando.com/en](https://spielerando.com/en)

  
It's for people with no prior software engineering knowledge, just install the mcp

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body:
I mean if you want to make on a factory line games this will do it. 

I think understanding of design and players is the most important part. Sure there are best practices, but it is way more important to understand the reason behind them, then actually know them. You can apply that knowledge to any design element later, so your game can be unique and it will feel like it follows the best practices even if there is non for that actual design element.

This is just my 2 cents on it. I looked on the site, it has many examples of things, but it has no cohesive learning curve for a human. 

It is basically stuff what you can ask ai and it would answer them.

If I would like to explore the best practices for a feature I would ask  something like this:  
“Do research and tell me the five best practices for this \[feature\] prefer information in publications from industry veterans or research papers. Your answer should contain why based on the sources. List the sources.”

However I would suggest reading some design books, because design is not just shaping features.

There are many user research papers out there.  If you use this webpage, you will use the biases of the content of single webpage.

replies.author: LegoFighter2
replies.body: You are absolutely, right. And I respect the sharpness of your though and that you share it here with me.
